title: Vector3
summary: A 3D point or direction: X, Y, Z. Positions, sizes, velocities, offsets — the fundamental spatial value. Supports arithmetic, Magnitude, Unit, Lerp, Dot/Cross products.

reference.signature: Vector3.new(x: number?, y: number?, z: number?) --> Vector3

methods.name: Magnitude / Unit
methods.description: Length of the vector / same direction with length 1.

methods.name: Dot / Cross
methods.description: Dot: alignment (-1..1 scaled by lengths). Cross: perpendicular vector.

methods.name: FuzzyEq
methods.description: Approximate equality — use instead of == for floats.

properties.name: X / Y / Z
properties.description: The three components. Y is UP in Roblox.

explanation.whatItIs: Three numbers with spatial meaning: where something is, which way it points, or how fast it moves.
explanation.whyItExists: A 3D world needs a 3D number. Everything spatial flows through Vector3.
whenNotToUse: When orientation matters too — CFrame combines position + rotation
Storing unrelated triples of numbers — a table is clearer
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Vector3.new(x, y, z)
        ↑        ↑
     sideways   Y is UP!

b - a           = vector from a to b
(b - a).Magnitude = distance between
(b - a).Unit      = direction a→b
```
tips: Distance WITHOUT sqrt: compare MagnitudeSquared against range² (faster)
Directions: always normalize with .Unit before scaling
Lerp for smooth follows: pos = pos:Lerp(goal, alpha)
commonMistakes: Using == for equality — float precision; use FuzzyEq or tolerance
Forgetting Y is up (not Z like some engines)
Adding to Position without considering orientation — CFrame math for facing-aware offsets

examples.title: Distance + direction idioms
examples.code:
local a = workspace.PartA.Position
local b = workspace.PartB.Position

local offset = b - a
local distance = offset.Magnitude
local direction = offset.Unit          -- normalized

print(`{distance} studs apart`)

if distance < 10 then
    print("Close!")
end

-- Move 5 studs toward B:
local step = a + direction * 5
